courses.title: Concepts of Criminal Law
courses.description: The course examines and evaluates the historical development, philosophy of law and constitutional provisions; definitions, classification of crime, and their application to the system of administration of justice. The course also evaluates the process of conducting legal research, the study of case law, methodology related to the development of criminal law, and concepts of law as a social force in a multicultural, multiethnic society.

courses.title: Interviewing, Interrogation and Crisis Intervention
courses.description: This course examines the theories, principles, and strategies of tactical and interpersonal communication necessary to interview victims, witnesses, and suspects. Students will explore crisis intervention strategies for victims and witnesses of crime, along with communication with individuals from diverse backgrounds with consideration to race, ethnicity, gender, age, and special needs.

courses.title: Federal Courts and Constitutional Law
courses.description: This course examines Federal court procedures and evaluates the impact of U.S. Constitutional law on federal and state law. The U.S. Constitution will be examined and analyzed to determine how it affects current U.S. Supreme Court case decisions and its interpretations of the Constitution and the Amendments.

courses.title: Law and Social Change
courses.description: The course will examine the exploration of the use of law as an instrument for social change within our society. The examination will enhance the analysis of the relationship between laws and social change in varied cross-cultural settings. The analysis of legislation, case law, the process of conflict resolution, and legal institutions will evaluate how these components relate to and influence the enactment of laws and social change.

courses.title: Trademarks Law
courses.description: This is an overview of the paralegal's role in trademark practice, including federal and foreign trademark registrations, prosecution of applications, maintenance, trademark clearance, and enforcement.

metadata.Advisory(ies): ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.
metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of what constitutes a Trademark and evidence of use of Trademarks. Demonstrate an understanding of the trademark clearance process and the paralegal's role in that process. Demonstrate an understanding of the paralegal's role in international trademark practice. Outline the appropriate procedures of the federal Trademark registration and maintenance process. Identify the rules and laws governing federal Trademark registration and options for enforcement.
